title: This app's settings file
description: GET and POST /v1/settings. The file is ~/.config/clawdline-next/config.json, never the Swift app's; its keys are the Swift app's spellings. A write is a merge onto what is on disk, atomic, and leaves every other key as it was. A file that is not a JSON object is refused rather than replaced. Website Settings is the primary entry. The narrow /v1/settings/default-models route carries launch defaults over the paired Cloud read/write path; retained settings window types remain compatible.

exists.description: False before anything has been written. Every key then has the shell's default.

path.description: Where the file is, whether or not it exists.

cloudflare_tunnel_retired.description: True while the file still holds the built-in Cloudflare tunnel's settings (`remote_tunnel`, `remote_tunnel_name`, `remote_hostname`, `cloudflared_path`), removed on 2026-10-20. They start nothing; the settings page explains once, and writing `cloudflare_tunnel_retired: false` takes them out of the file.

hotkey.description: The file's `hotkey`, or null when the file does not carry one as a string. Null means the default, option+space, which the Swift app used to own and no longer does; an empty string means the person asked for none, and registers nothing.

scope_app.description: The file's `scope_app`, or null when absent — which the shell reads as com.googlecode.iterm2. Empty is every app.

language.description: Existing agent and Board authoring language and voice auto fallback. Its stored value and behavior are preserved independently of product language.

product_language.description: Daemon notifications and human-readable CLI copy. Absent, malformed or unsupported saved values render as English.

mascot.description: Which mascot pack the shell draws.

terminal.description: Where a new session opens: `auto`, `iterm`, `iterm_native` or `tmux`. With tmux installed, `auto` and `iterm` run the session in tmux and show it in an iTerm2 tab; `iterm_native` runs it in the tab itself. Not the same question as scope_app.

antigravity_default_model.description: Native Antigravity model slug. Empty leaves the choice to Antigravity; no fallback to another provider.

antigravity_default_effort.description: Native Antigravity effort: low, medium, high, xhigh or max. Empty leaves the choice to Antigravity.

codex_default_effort.description: Codex reasoning effort for new Sessions when the launch does not name one. Empty leaves the choice to Codex.

codex_default_model.description: The model used for a new Codex session when that launch does not name one. Empty leaves the choice to Codex.

claude_default_model.description: The model used for a new Claude Code session when that launch does not name one. Empty leaves the choice to Claude Code.

reopen_on_return.description: Whether the bar comes back with the terminal.

follow_target.description: Whether the terminal selects the tab the bar points at.

codex_auto_name.description: Whether a new session is named by an assistant. The Swift app's spelling, kept so a line copied between the two files means the same thing.

auto_name_assistant.description: Whose quota that naming turn spends, `claude` or `codex`. Remembered while the switch above is off, so turning it back on does not quietly change providers.

notch.description: Whether a mascot lives in the notch.

y_fraction.description: Where the bar's top sits, as a fraction of screen height.

output_mode.description: What the reading pane shows: `auto`, `transcript` or `terminal`.

output_height.description: The reading pane's height in points.

output_size.description: The reading pane's text size in points.

output_font.description: The reading pane's face. Monospaced, because the pane draws a terminal.

backdrop.description: How much the bar blurs what is behind it.

output_newest_first.description: Whether the reading pane puts the newest first.

voice_language.description: What whisper reads a recording as: `auto`, which follows `language`, then this machine's languages, then the shipped catalog — or a tag such as `zh-Hant`, `zh-Hans` or `en`.

voice_settle_seconds.description: How long a pause ends a sentence. 0 is off.

voice_stop_seconds.description: How long a silence ends the whole turn. 0 is off.

remote.description: Whether anything but this Mac may read the session list.

tailscale_hostname.description: This machine's full Tailscale name (`<machine>.<tailnet>.ts.net`) that Tailscale Serve answers on; accepted only while `remote` is on.

push_on_delivery.description: Notify when a session reports a delivery.

push_on_fanout.description: Notify when a whole batch of dispatched work ends.

smart_notifications.description: Have a model write the sentence a notification carries.

push_on_deploy.description: Notify when a deploy ends, either way.

push_on_waiting.description: Notify when a Session waits for the person.

push_on_board_decision.description: Notify when a Board decision needs an answer.

push_on_board_done.description: Notify when a Board item is completed.

push_on_schedule_failure.description: Notify when a schedule fails or its file is unreadable.

push_on_capacity.description: Notify when a capacity threshold is crossed.

push_on_dead_letter.description: Notify when a task completion cannot reach its Session.

push_on_app_release_success.description: Notify after the app release is verified.

push_on_cloud_release_success.description: Notify after the Cloud release is verified.

push_on_release_failure.description: Notify when an App install or Cloud verification fails.

cloud_health_upload.description: Whether this daemon uploads its connection-health records to Cloud. Absent or false means off, and off makes no request. Only the local token may change it. Owner diagnostics (location, age, deadline) are never sent.

cloud_health_owner_retention.description: Whether this daemon keeps owner diagnostics (location, age, deadline) in Cloud as ciphertext only paired owner devices can open. Separate from cloud_health_upload, which never permits it. Absent or false means off, and off makes no request. Only the local token may change it.

orchestrator_agent_notify.description: Whether an agent may push a sentence of its own.

iterm_integration.description: Explicit opt-in to reading and controlling iTerm2; absent is off, including existing installations.

iterm_scan.description: Legacy polling preference inside an explicitly enabled iterm_integration. Absent means true. This preference never grants integration consent. Off, background listing and screen sampling stop; requested actions are allowed only while integration is enabled.

planning_gate.description: Whether a newly assigned execution cycle captures the planning gate. Absent means true; a later setting change never rewrites an in-flight cycle's snapshot.

verify_gate.description: Whether a newly assigned execution cycle captures independent verification. Absent means false; a later setting change never rewrites an in-flight cycle's snapshot.

orchestrator_enabled.description: Whether one session may hand work to another.

orchestrator_max_children.description: How many child sessions one session may run at once, 1 to 10.

orchestrator_permission.description: How far a child may go on its own: `ask`, `edits` or `full`.

orchestrator_notify_root.description: Whether a finished child types a line back into the session that sent it.

orchestrator_child_linger.description: What becomes of a child's tab after it reports: 0 closes it, 180 waits three minutes, -1 keeps it.

claude_auto_compact_window.description: The context size, in tokens, at which the Claude sessions this daemon opens — children, Root Assignments, handoffs — compact their history into a summary. Null or 0 is none, the default: Claude Code then compacts only near its own window. A task.json's `auto_compact_window` overrides it for one task. Never given to Codex, or to a session the person opened.

update_auto_apply.description: Whether this machine installs a newer stable release by itself when no session it started is busy (docs/updates.md). Only a release install acts on it. Null or absent is off, the default.

on_state_change.description: The file's `on_state_change`, the argv this app runs when a session changes state. Read only here: it is an argument list, not a command line, and a single text box invites exactly the word-splitting that would break a path with a space in it. Absent is an empty list.

SettingsRequest.description: The keys to change. A null key is left as it is.

hotkey.description: A combination the shell can register (`cmd+shift+k`), or empty for none.

scope_app.description: Bundle identifiers separated by commas, or empty for every app.

language.description: Existing agent and Board authoring language and voice auto fallback.

product_language.description: One of the nine shipped product-copy tags; changes daemon notifications and human-readable CLI copy only.

mascot.description: A pack name the shell offers.

antigravity_default_model.description: Native Antigravity model slug. Empty leaves the choice to Antigravity; no fallback to another provider.

antigravity_default_effort.description: Native Antigravity effort: low, medium, high, xhigh or max. Empty leaves the choice to Antigravity.

codex_default_effort.description: Empty, high or xhigh for a new Codex Session.

codex_default_model.description: Empty, or a Codex model name used when a new Session does not name one.

claude_default_model.description: Empty, or a Claude Code model name used when a new Session does not name one.

reopen_on_return.description: Whether the bar comes back with the terminal.

follow_target.description: Whether the terminal selects the tab the bar points at.

codex_auto_name.description: Whether a new session is named by an assistant.

notch.description: Whether a mascot lives in the notch.

output_newest_first.description: Whether the reading pane puts the newest first.

voice_language.description: `auto`, or a language tag: letters, digits and dashes.

remote.description: Whether anything but this Mac may read the session list.

tailscale_hostname.description: A full Tailscale name ending in `.ts.net`, or empty.

cloudflare_tunnel_retired.description: Only `false`: dismisses the retired Cloudflare tunnel notice by removing that tunnel's old keys from the file. The old keys themselves are refused as `retired_setting`.

WorkGateSettingsSnapshot.description: The two machine-wide gate values shown by every console. These are defaults for future successful assignments; an in-flight cycle keeps its captured pair.

WorkGateSettingsRequest.description: A narrow change to the gate defaults. A missing or null key leaves that value unchanged.
